messages:
maria: Heads-up — on Friday's deploy I see a ~12% p95 increase for hosted inference on small requests (<=64 tokens). Quick profile attached. 

maria: Flame sample shows a big chunk in a host-side stage we haven't tracked carefully: 'scanline token sorter' (part of preparse/tokenize pipeline) — lots of memcpy + syscalls right before we hand to kernel selector.

sam: ugh. is that the new scanline reorder patch? 

maria: yes, merged in PR #4821. The hot path is effectively doing per-request sorting for prefix alignment. Here's the short stack from perf top: 
```
scanline_token_sorter::sort_range
tokenize::emit_fragment
host_preparse::handle_stream
grpc::writev
syscall::writev
```

akash: interesting that writev shows up — maybe smallwrites are not coalescing. Can you paste the ingress header counts?

maria: pasted minimal sample below (from trace logs): 
```
req=13ms p50, 120ms p95
writev_calls/request ~4.1 (baseline ~1.2)
avg fragments per req 3.7 -> 4.9 post-PR
KV cache hit-rate unchanged
"sort" CPU ~22% of preparse CPU
```

lisa: KV hit-rate unchanged but fragments per request up suggests we are splitting streams earlier or adding headers. Does the sorter create extra fragment boundaries?

maria: yes — sorter aligns tokens to 32B scanlines; that produces extra small fragments when upstream framed payloads are already chunked. We do a memcpy to a temporary vector and then emit. Combined with multiple writev calls, it amplifies syscall overhead.

sam: could we make sorter operate in-place (stable partition) and only allocate when fragmentation actually increases? Or run as a post-coalesce step after writev coalesce?

akash: Another angle: batching heuristics. If host-side preparse increments fragments, batching becomes less efficient because our batching key uses fragment-count heuristic. We should consider switching to a pre-token-count histogram for batch windows. That avoids sticking small fragments into separate batches.

perf-bot: Canary results: canary-2026-03-20 shows 11.8% p95 latency regress vs baseline, CPU up 9% on preparse.

maria: quick experiment — disabled scanline reorder in canary and p95 regressed back to baseline. So it's the culprit. 

lisa: We should also consider KV cache interaction: more fragments => more unique prefixes => more KV churn. Even if static hit-rate didn't move in the short sample, I bet with steady load eviction churn appears later.

akash: proposed quick fixes: 
1) Make sorter lazy: only allocate copy when alignment would increase fragments_count > 1.
2) Coalesce small fragments at write path before writev (merge adjacent small buffers).
3) Adjust batching key to use pre-token-length bucket rather than fragments.

maria: I implemented 1) and 2) locally — smoke looks promising. Locally p95 back to -3% and writev_calls/request down to ~1.4. I'll push a prototype branch for review: `maria/scanline-lazy-coalesce`.

sam: can you include a microbenchmark for the allocator path? We need numbers for copy vs in-place penalties. 

maria: yes — added simple harness: 
```
// micro: simulate 64B chunks, alignment to 32B
for i in 0..1e6 {
  if needs_align(buf) { tmp = copy_and_align(buf) } else { in_place_align(buf) }
}
```
results: copy path 3.9x slower but only hit for ~18% of samples in real traces.

akash: ok that's reasonable. For batching change we should be careful: affects autoscaler/utilization math. Maybe rollout as canary for 24h and compare throughput/cost.

lisa: also add a KV-cache diagnostic: sample per-shard eviction rates over 6h. If eviction rises after day 1 we'll need a hot-set pin or two-tier approach.

maria: plan for next steps: 
- open PR with lazy sorter + writev coalesce (small, isolated).
- add batch-key opt-in flag and canary it (48h).
- add per-shard eviction telemetry to perf dashboard.
- run full end-to-end canary (baseline, proto, opt-in) and collect p50/p95, CPU, writev counts, kv-evict.

sam: LGTM. Please @akash for batching changes. I'll review the sorter PR. :thumbsup:

akash: will watch canary and run sim on batching. If it looks good we can ship both in a single minor release.

maria: thanks — I'll post the PR link in this thread when ready. If anyone wants the raw flame/profile I uploaded to GCS: gs://redwood-perf/1791234560/scanline-flame.svg

lisa: ping me once metrics are in, I'll check KV eviction.

maria: will do.
